meta.title: Italy 2026
meta.subtitle: Rome · Florence · Tuscany · Sorrento & the Amalfi Coast
meta.arrival: FCO Mon Aug 24, 11:50am (ITA Airways from IAH)
meta.routeLine: Rome (3) → Florence (2) → Castelfalfi (2) → Sorrento (5) → Rome finale (1)
meta.transportLine: Private driver in from FCO · Frecciarossa to Florence · self-drive Florence–Castelfalfi only (Aug 29–31) · rail to Naples, Campania Express over to Sorrento · ferries to Capri, Positano and Amalfi · Frecciarossa back to Rome
meta.chainStory: Hotel Trame (Rome, independent) → The Hoxton, Florence (Ennismore) → Il Castelfalfi (Tuscany, TUI Blue Selection) → Ara Maris Hotel & Spa (Sorrento) → Nomos Hotel (Rome, DNA Hotels)

days.title: Landing in Rome
days.kicker: ROME — Hotel Trame, by the Pantheon
days.note: Twenty hours awake by the time you land, so nothing here is timed and the only thing worth booking is the Pantheon. The walk, the shops and dinner all sit within fifteen minutes of Trame, so any of them can be dropped without wrecking the rest. Eat in tonight — food carried back beats sitting in a restaurant on day one.

items.title: Land at FCO
items.detail: Immigration + bags, about 45 min

items.title: Uber to Hotel Trame
items.detail: Uber it is, but know what that means here: Italy has no UberX, so the app books Uber Black and it runs dearer than a cab. The official FCO flat rate into the centre is €55 from the rank straight outside arrivals, and itTaxi or FreeNow call the same metered cars. Either way licensed cars may enter the ZTL, so you are dropped at the hotel door rather than a street away.

items.title: Check in at Hotel Trame
items.detail: Via Monterone 22, 00186 Roma — a former Franciscan monastery with the cloister still in the middle, rooms ready from 2:00pm. It sits 230m below the Pantheon rather than beside Campo de' Fiori, which is 350m the other way. The hotel line is +39 06 8115 3856 if a driver cannot find the lane.

items.title: Heart of Rome Walk (1–3 hours)
items.detail: Rick Steves' route, in order: Campo de' Fiori, Piazza Navona, the Pantheon, Piazza di Montecitorio, then the Trevi Fountain. Campo de' Fiori is 350m from the hotel door, five minutes, and the Trevi end is five more from the shops — so the whole afternoon chains together on foot with no taxi. Take it at whatever pace the jet lag allows — an hour if you march it, three if you stop.

items.title: Shopping: Via del Corso up to the Spanish Steps
items.detail: Via del Corso runs from Piazza Venezia to Piazza del Popolo; Via dei Condotti at the top is the luxury row. Monday hours, so shops open about 3:30–4pm and shut at 7:30–8pm. Small independents may still be closed for August.

items.title: Dinner in — food carried back to Trame
items.detail: No restaurant on night one: one of you walks out and brings dinner back. Emma, the Roscioli family's pizzeria, is about five minutes away and will box it up; the alimentari around the Pantheon are closer still. Twenty hours awake is the whole reason.

days.title: The Vatican, gardens first
days.note: Booked: the Vatican's own Gardens and Museums tour at 8:30, not the early-entry tour first planned. The gardens are guided-visit only, so few Museums visitors see them — but this does not buy an empty Sistine Chapel, and St Peter's is not part of it. Be at Viale Vaticano by eight with ID and the voucher. The afternoon is reordered so the castle follows lunch instead of a taxi home and back — it is ten minutes from the Vatican, and the old shape crossed Rome twice for nothing.

items.title: Vatican Gardens and Museums — arrive 8:00am, tour at 8:30am
items.detail: Show the voucher to Customer Care outside the Viale Vaticano entrance, 30 minutes before. After security, take the stairs at the far left of the hall to the Guided Tours desk for tickets, then on to the meeting point for earphones. Entrance is Passageway 2, and both names on the ticket are checked against ID.

items.title: Quick lunch in Borgo
items.detail: Borgo Pio is the pedestrian lane between the Vatican walls and the castle, which is exactly where you need to be next. Anywhere with a free table will do — this is a stop, not an occasion.
items.how: Walk, ~10 min from the museum exit

items.title: Castel Sant'Angelo, then Ponte Sant'Angelo
items.detail: Ten minutes from where you just ate, which is the point — the old plan sent you back to the hotel at half two and out again at five, crossing the city twice to reach somewhere you were already standing next to. Spiral ramp up to the roof terrace for the view back over St Peter's. Bernini's angels are on the bridge as you leave.

items.title: Back east on foot through the centro storico
items.detail: Cross the river and walk home the long way — Via dei Coronari, Piazza Navona, whatever you missed yesterday. Half an hour direct, or all afternoon if you graze. It lands you near the hotel with time to change.

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo near Campo de' Fiori
items.detail: Anywhere with a roof and a spritz — you are eating properly after the opera, so this is a drink and not a meal.

items.title: OPERA — arias at All Saints' Anglican Church
items.detail: Via del Babuino, off Piazza di Spagna. The Aug 25 programme is still unconfirmed and nothing is booked — that is now top of the booking list, not a maybe.

items.title: Late dinner — Pierluigi
items.detail: Seafood on Piazza de' Ricci, at a properly Roman hour. Six minutes from the hotel. The least fixed thing on the day — swap it for anywhere still serving if you would rather.

days.title: Ancient Rome, then the Borghese
days.note: Last full Roman day. Everything hangs off the booked 1:00pm Galleria Borghese entry, meeting point 12:45pm, so the morning has to finish before then. Lunch is quick in Monti, and the shaded hour in the gardens afterwards replaces the siesta.

items.title: Baths of Caracalla
items.detail: Go first, while it is quiet — far emptier than anything else in ancient Rome at this hour. Brick vaults at full height, huge bathing halls, patches of the original mosaic floor.

items.title: The Colosseum from outside, and the Arch of Constantine
items.detail: The outside circuit from the Via dei Fori Imperiali side, then the Arch of Constantine. No interior ticket, so nothing to book and no queue.

items.title: Quick lunch in Monti
items.detail: Quick by necessity: the Borghese meeting point is a fifteen-minute taxi away and will not hold, so eat by 12:10. Roscioli had this slot but wants two unhurried hours. Give it another lunch rather than rush it.

items.title: Galleria Borghese — meet 12:45pm, entry at 1:00pm
items.detail: Meet the host at the Fontana dei Mascheroni, in front of the gallery — purple Crown Tours shirt and a flag. Bring ID, your own headphones and a charged phone. No large bags inside, but the cloakroom is free.

items.title: Villa Borghese Gardens
items.detail: Straight out of the gallery into the park. Shaded avenues, the Fontana dei Cavalli Marini, and a bench under the pines through the worst of the heat.

items.title: The Pincio terrace, in the low sun
items.detail: The terrace over Piazza del Popolo, St. Peter's dome on the skyline. This is the Rome photo session, timed for the low sun through the trees.

items.title: Down to Piazza del Popolo
items.detail: The twin churches and the obelisk, down the Pincio steps

items.title: Trastevere on foot
items.detail: Cross the Tiber and wander to Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere

items.title: Dinner — Da Enzo al 29
items.detail: Trastevere, twelve tables, no reservations after 9pm

days.title: North to Florence, and straight into it
days.changeNote: Florence now comes second, right after Rome, and the day starts at checkout rather than dragging you out at dawn — the last Roman morning is yours.
days.note: Check out at eleven, and Florence still gets the afternoon and evening. The booked train is the 12:10, in at 2:11pm, with lunch on board in Executive; check in properly on arrival so the afternoon runs with nothing to carry. One fixed point after that — the dome climb at 4:30pm sharp, unmovable and ID-checked, so if the train runs late drop the Accademia, not the dome.

items.title: Check out — Hotel Trame; taxi to Termini
items.detail: Checkout is eleven and Termini is about fifteen minutes by taxi from Via Monterone. No need to be up early — have a last coffee on the piazza.

items.title: Frecciarossa 9420 to Florence
items.detail: Booked: Roma Termini 12:10 → Firenze S.M.N. 14:11, Executive, coach 1. Base fare, so it can be changed any number of times before departure.

items.title: Check in — The Hoxton
items.detail: Via delle Mantellate 2, up by San Marco — 1.3km from the platform, so take a taxi with the bags. Rooms are ready from 2:00pm, so check in properly now rather than dropping bags and coming back for them. Checkout the 29th at noon, room-only, so breakfast is on you.

items.title: Accademia — David, if the day allows
items.detail: Optional, and the first thing to drop if the train runs late. Book the 3:00pm entry anyway, and be walking out by 4:15 or you are gambling with the dome. Forty-five minutes is enough — go straight down the hall of the Prisoners.

items.title: Climb Brunelleschi's dome — 4:30pm sharp
items.detail: Entry is at the Porta della Mandorla — be there by 4:15 with ID, as the slot cannot be changed. 463 steps, no lift. The same pass covers the Bell Tower, Baptistery, museum and crypt through 29 August.

items.title: Back to the room to change
items.detail: You checked in on arrival, so this is only a shower and a change before dinner. You will want it after 463 steps.

items.title: Ponte Vecchio, then up to Piazzale Michelangelo
items.detail: Sunset is about 8:00pm and the hill is where to watch it. Taxi up, walk down through the rose garden.

items.title: Dinner — Borgo San Jacopo
items.detail: Michelin-starred, on the river, with a few window tables. Ask for one.

days.title: Boboli at opening, the Uffizi, and back through the Renaissance
days.note: The only full Florence day, and a dense one. Two ticketed slots hold it together: Pitti the minute it opens and the Uffizi at 12:15, with Boboli first because the heat makes it unwalkable later. Thursday's Duomo pass is still live so the museum is free, but it cannot get you the cathedral nave — 10:15am–3:45pm Mon–Sat only, and nothing here fits.

items.title: Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens
items.detail: 8:15 is when the gates open, and that is the point — Boboli is terraced, unshaded and unwalkable by mid-afternoon. The Palatine Gallery is hung floor to ceiling in the old manner. Climb to the top of the gardens for the view back over the city.

items.title: Coffee on the way down to Ponte Vecchio
items.detail: Via de' Guicciardini runs from the palace gates to the bridge. Stop halfway.

items.title: Uffizi, guided
items.detail: Botticelli, Leonardo, the Caravaggio room. About two hours with a guide.

items.title: Late lunch — 'Ino
items.detail: The Uffizi puts you out at 2:30, when Oltrarno kitchens stop serving, so lunch is thirty seconds from the gallery door. Panini made to order, Tuscan wine by the glass, open through the afternoon. Il Santo Bevitore is the sit-down alternative if the tour runs short.

items.title: Reverse Renaissance Walk
items.detail: The centre backwards: Casa di Dante, Orsanmichele, then Piazza della Signoria and the Loggia dei Lanzi — an open-air sculpture hall, free.

items.title: Opera del Duomo museum
items.detail: Already paid: Thursday's Brunelleschi Pass runs to the 29th. Ghiberti's original Gates of Paradise and Michelangelo's late Pietà, at Piazza del Duomo 9.

items.title: Back to the hotel to change
items.detail: Fifteen minutes uphill from the centre — taxi if the day has run long

items.title: OPERA — La Traviata at St. Mark's Anglican
items.detail: Via Maggio, across Ponte Santa Trinita. A chamber staging in a small church, closer to the singers than an opera house puts you.

items.title: Dinner — Trattoria Sostanza
items.detail: Cash only. The butter chicken and the tortino. Alternative: Buca dell'Orafo.

days.title: Up to Fiesole, then into the Val d'Elsa
days.changeNote: The rental car is collected here and returned in Florence on Aug 31 — two days of driving in the whole trip, and none of it in a city centre.

items.title: Check out; collect the rental car
items.detail: The agencies are on Borgo Ognissanti, outside the ZTL, so you never drive into the centro storico. Twenty minutes downhill from the Hoxton, so taxi with the luggage. Have the IDP and licence ready.

items.title: Fiesole — Florence from the hill
items.detail: Twenty-five minutes up for the view back over the city — roofs, river and dome from above. Go out along the viali to stay clear of the ZTL, and park at Piazza Mino.

items.title: Southwest to Certaldo
items.detail: An hour and ten from Fiesole, against forty-five minutes driving straight out. That is what the view costs, and Certaldo still gets an hour before lunch.

items.title: Certaldo Alto, by funicular
items.detail: Boccaccio's birthplace, a walled brick town. The funicular climbs from Piazza Boccaccio in under two minutes

items.title: Casa Boccaccio
items.detail: The Decameron's author was born here; the house is now a small, quiet museum

items.title: Lunch on Via Boccaccio
items.detail: A terrace table in the upper town before the drive on

items.title: On to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes further into the Val d'Elsa

items.title: Check in — Il Castelfalfi
items.detail: A restored 14th-century hamlet on a 2,700-acre estate, with its own castle. Deluxe Room with breakfast. Rooms from 3:00pm, checkout 11:00am on the 31st.

items.title: The hamlet on foot
items.detail: The piazza, the castle walls, the little church — all restored, none of it roped off

items.title: Aperitivo at Ecrù
items.detail: The estate's cocktail bar

items.title: Dinner — La Via del Sale
items.detail: The estate's fine-dining room; the vegetables and olive oil are grown on the property

days.title: Towers, then on horseback through the vines
days.kicker: TUSCANY — San Gimignano and a horseback vineyard tour
days.note: One day for both San Gimignano and the horseback vineyard tour. Tuscany is only two nights, so Volterra and a separate wine estate do not fit.

items.title: Drive to San Gimignano
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes

items.title: The towers of San Gimignano
items.detail: Fourteen of the original seventy-two medieval towers still stand. Best seen from Piazza della Cisterna

items.title: The Collegiata
items.detail: Ghirlandaio and Gozzoli frescoes wall to wall in a church the size of a chapel

items.title: Gelato at Dondoli
items.detail: A two-time world gelato champion on Piazza della Cisterna. Quick, before the horses

items.title: Horseback riding, lunch and a winery
items.detail: Meets at the Bivio Volterra bus stop, 11am to 3pm. An hour in the saddle, then lunch, a cellar tour and tastings. No riding experience needed; backup operator is CET Experience, cetexperience.it.
items.how: Meet at the Bivio Volterra bus stop

items.title: Back to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes

items.title: Pool or spa terrace
items.detail: You've earned it after a day in the saddle

items.title: Dinner — La Via del Sale
items.detail: The estate's fine-dining room, on your last Tuscan night

days.title: The long haul south, to one bed for five nights
days.kicker: TUSCANY → SORRENTO — car back to Florence, rail to Naples, driver over the peninsula
days.changeNote: The longest travel day of the trip, and the last one — everything after this is a day trip from a single base. One of you is working remotely from Aug 31 to Sep 5, so the coast is now one hotel rather than three.
days.note: Three legs back to back, but the trains are booked and the last leaves from the building you arrive in, so nothing depends on Naples traffic. You reach the hotel about 6:50pm.

items.title: Check out; on the road
items.detail: Back toward Florence, retracing Saturday's route. The booked train is the 1:14pm, so there is no need for a dawn start.

items.title: Drop off the rental car
items.detail: Borgo Ognissanti — the two-day rental ends where it started

items.title: Lunch by the station before the train
items.detail: The later train buys an unhurried hour, and the next real meal is dinner in Sorrento

items.title: Frecciarossa 9587 to Naples
items.detail: Booked: Firenze S.M.N. 13:14 → Napoli Centrale 16:23, direct via Rome, Executive, coach 1. The longest leg of the trip.

items.title: Arrive Napoli Centrale
items.detail: Stay in the building — the Circumvesuviana platforms are downstairs, signed EAV

items.title: Campania Express to Sorrento
items.detail: EAV 17:26 → Sorrento 18:35, direct. Platforms are downstairs from the Frecciarossa, signed EAV — no crossing Naples with the bags. Reserved seats, air conditioning and room for a suitcase.

items.title: Arrive Sorrento station
items.detail: The hotel is 480m away, six minutes on the flat. That is why this beats the ferry — Marina Piccola is the same distance uphill

items.title: Check in — Ara Maris Hotel & Spa
items.detail: Via Correale 15, a few minutes east of Piazza Tasso. Deluxe Sea View for the first four nights. Ask the desk to move the room on the 4th while you are out at Amalfi.

items.title: Unpack — this is home for five nights
items.detail: The gardens and the elliptical pool can wait for tomorrow; tonight is just arriving

items.title: Aperitivo at the Lumi Sky Lounge
items.detail: The hotel's rooftop bar — Vesuvius on the far shore, and it goes pink at sunset

items.title: Dinner — Cora Bistrot
items.detail: The hotel's own Mediterranean room — the easiest first night after three legs. Book before you arrive.

days.title: Sorrento, at walking pace
days.kicker: SORRENTO — the town, the lemon groves, and the first desk day
days.changeNote: New. Built around the work-from-home week — mornings are the trip, afternoons from about 2:30pm are held open for the desk.
days.note: Every coast day is shaped the same: the outing runs morning to early afternoon, you are back by 7pm, and dinner is at the hotel or a few minutes away. That holds all five nights, with the Ravello day on Sep 4 the only tight one. If you are working European hours, move the desk block to the morning.

items.title: Breakfast in the garden
items.detail: Under the lemon and orange trees — the reason people book this hotel

items.title: Sorrento on foot
items.detail: Piazza Tasso, the shopfronts of Via San Cesareo, and the Vallone dei Mulini — a fern-covered ruined mill in a gorge in the middle of town

items.title: I Giardini di Cataldo
items.detail: A working lemon and orange grove in the centre of town, free to walk through, with limoncello made on site

items.title: Lunch at Marina Grande — Bagni Delfino
items.detail: A wooden deck over the water in the old fishing village below town. Fritto misto and a carafe of white.

items.title: Desk hours
items.detail: Fibre in the rooms. The garden terrace is the quiet spot if the room feels small by day three.

items.title: The pool, or the Thala Spa
items.detail: No lift down to the water here. The hotel works with a beach club at the marina — ask the desk to book it the night before

items.title: Dinner — O'Parrucchiano La Favorita
items.detail: Tables among the lemon trees of a 19th-century greenhouse. Cannelloni was invented in this kitchen, so order it. Six minutes from the door.

days.title: Capri, twenty-five minutes away
days.changeNote: Capri is now a short hop rather than an expedition — the crossing from Sorrento is 25 minutes against about 50 from Naples, which buys back most of a morning.
days.note: Weather-dependent. The Blue Grotto only opens in a flat sea — treat it as a bonus, not a plan. Buy the return leg when you buy the outbound.

items.title: Down to Marina Piccola
items.detail: Twenty minutes on foot, and the last stretch is steep. The public lift from the Villa Comunale gardens skips it, or take a taxi

items.title: Fast ferry — Sorrento → Capri
items.detail: About 25 minutes. Up to forty crossings a day in season, but they sell out at the counter in August — book online the night before.

items.title: Round-the-island boat from Marina Grande
items.detail: The Faraglioni, the grottoes and the swim coves, plus the Blue Grotto if the sea is calm enough. About two hours.

items.title: Lunch — Da Paolino
items.detail: Under the lemon trees. Il Riccio is the Michelin alternative, on the cliff by the grotto.

items.title: The Piazzetta and the Gardens of Augustus
items.detail: Gelato on the terrace above Via Krupp, looking straight down at the Faraglioni

items.title: Ferry back to Sorrento
items.detail: Check the last sailing when you land. Missing it means a night on the island

items.title: Desk hours
items.detail: Back at the hotel with the US afternoon still ahead

items.title: Dinner — Il Buco
items.detail: Michelin-starred, in the wine cellar of an old monastery just off Piazza Tasso

days.title: Positano, for an afternoon
days.kicker: SORRENTO → POSITANO — by ferry, there and back
days.changeNote: New. Positano gets its own half-day by sea instead of being glimpsed from a passing ferry.
days.note: Positano has no real port, just a pier that closes in rough weather, so check the morning update if the forecast looks unsettled. The town is almost entirely stairs — wear the right shoes.

items.title: Slow morning — swim and breakfast
items.detail: No ticket, no departure to make until mid-morning

items.title: Ferry to Positano
items.detail: About 35 minutes down the peninsula. Mid-April to mid-October only; book the day before in August.

items.title: Positano from the water, then from the stairs
items.detail: The pastel town stacked straight up from Spiaggia Grande, under the majolica dome of Santa Maria Assunta. The best picture is from the boat coming in, so have the camera out before you dock.

items.title: Lunch — Chez Black, on the beach
items.detail: Right on Spiaggia Grande, and unpretentious despite the address. La Tagliata up in the hills is the alternative if you would rather climb.

items.title: Via Pasitea and the boutiques
items.detail: Linen and sandals made to measure while you wait — the town's real local industry

items.title: Golden hour on the Villa Comunale terrace
items.detail: A public balcony on the cliff edge, three minutes from the hotel, over the Bay of Naples. The light goes gold about an hour before the sun drops behind Ischia.

items.title: Dinner — Ristorante Museo Caruso
items.detail: A block off Piazza Tasso, walls covered in Caruso memorabilia. The seafood is better than the theme suggests

days.title: Amalfi below, Ravello above
days.kicker: SORRENTO → AMALFI & RAVELLO — ferry down, driver up, driver home
days.changeNote: Amalfi and Ravello are now a single day trip from the Sorrento base rather than a two-night stay — which is what makes the five-night work week possible.
days.note: The room changes today — Deluxe Sea View out at 11:00am, Superior in at 3:00pm — but you leave at 8:15am and are not back until 6:30pm, so settle it at the desk the night before and let them move the bags. Leave Ravello by 5pm to be back by 6:30. The Ravello Festival runs to Sep 5, so tonight's Villa Rufolo concert is an option — worth breaking the 7pm rule for, but a 1h30 drive back near midnight.

items.title: Down to Marina Piccola
items.detail: Taxi this one. It is the earliest start of the five and the walk is twenty minutes downhill

items.title: Ferry to Amalfi, via Positano
items.detail: About 40 minutes direct, a little over an hour with the Positano call. Mid-April to mid-October only.

items.title: Amalfi's Duomo and the Cloister of Paradise
items.detail: The striped façade of Sant'Andrea, up sixty-two steps, with a 13th-century cloister of Arab-Norman arches behind it

items.title: The lemon lanes behind the piazza
items.detail: Up the Valle dei Mulini path. Amalfi made paper here for six hundred years and the ruined mills are still in the gorge

items.title: Lunch — Da Gemma
items.detail: Just off Piazza Duomo, on a terrace above the street. The best table in Amalfi

items.title: Private driver up to Ravello
items.detail: Thirty minutes of switchbacks, a thousand feet straight up from the coast

items.title: Villa Cimbrone
items.detail: The Terrace of Infinity: a marble balustrade lined with busts, and a thousand-foot drop to the sea

items.title: Villa Rufolo's gardens
items.detail: Wagner's Klingsor garden, and the festival stage cantilevered out over the drop

items.title: Driver back to Sorrento
items.detail: Over the pass rather than around the coast — about an hour and a half either way. Leaving at five puts you back at the hotel by 6:30pm.

items.title: Dinner — L'Antica Trattoria
items.detail: Under a pergola in the old town. The last proper dinner on the coast

days.title: Back to Rome for the last night
days.kicker: SORRENTO → ROME — driver to Naples, then the Frecciarossa
days.changeNote: The finale hotel moved from Via Vittorio Veneto down to the Regola, four minutes off Campo de' Fiori — so the last afternoon is the old centre on foot rather than the Dolce Vita end of town. It also puts you back in the quarter you started in, two streets from Hotel Trame.

items.title: Check out — Ara Maris
items.detail: Checkout is 11:00am, so this is early by choice. It buys the Naples stop below

items.title: Campania Express to Naples
items.detail: Sorrento 10:20 → Napoli Piazza Garibaldi 11:34, direct. Piazza Garibaldi is Napoli Centrale, so you step off one train where the next leaves.

items.title: Arrive Napoli Centrale
items.detail: Nearly two hours before the Frecciarossa, and the point of the early start

items.title: Pizza in Naples — the thing the replan took away
items.detail: Bags into the station deposit, then the old city — Di Matteo and Sorbillo are twenty minutes up Via dei Tribunali. Naples came out of the itinerary altogether, and this is the one window it gets back. If you would rather not risk it, there is good pizza in sight of the station.

items.title: Frecciarossa 9544 to Rome
items.detail: Booked. Napoli Centrale 13:30 → Roma Termini 14:55, Executive, coach 1.

items.title: Arrive Roma Termini; taxi to the hotel
Check in — Nomos Hotel
items.detail: Via di San Paolo alla Regola, four minutes from Campo de' Fiori and two streets from where the trip began. Superior Double, and nothing is prepaid — you settle €530 with the hotel.

items.title: The Jewish Ghetto and the Portico d'Ottavia
items.detail: Six minutes from the door, and the one corner of the centre you have not walked. Europe's oldest standing Jewish quarter, with the ruined portico built into the street

items.title: Tiber Island and the Ponte Fabricio
items.detail: The bridge has carried people since 62 BC, still on the original stone

items.title: Trevi Fountain, one last time
items.detail: Twenty minutes up through the centre. Worth the crowd on a last evening

items.title: Aperitivo on Campo de' Fiori
items.detail: The market stalls are packed away by now and the square turns over to drinking

items.title: Farewell dinner — Aroma, at Palazzo Manfredi
items.detail: Michelin-starred, on a rooftop looking straight into the Colosseum. Book early — only a dozen tables have the view.

items.title: Taxi to FCO
items.detail: About thirty-five minutes on an empty Sunday road. No rental to return; that ended in Florence on Aug 31.

items.title: Check in and bag drop
items.detail: Three hours ahead for an intercontinental departure

items.title: FCO → IAH
items.detail: Arrivederci, Italia.

hotels.name: Hotel Trame
hotels.blurb: A former Franciscan monastery on Via Monterone, a couple of minutes below the Pantheon. Confirmed.

hotels.name: The Hoxton, Florence
hotels.blurb: A 16th-century palazzo with a vaulted arcade, up in San Marco rather than by the station. Confirmed — Studio Terrace, room only, no breakfast, free cancellation until the day before. €574 goes on the card; the €28 city tax is paid at the property.

hotels.name: Il Castelfalfi
hotels.blurb: A restored 14th-century hamlet on a 2,700-acre estate, with Tuscany's largest golf course and its own vineyards. Confirmed — Deluxe Room, breakfast for two, free cancellation. $2,108.92 is charged on Aug 24; the remaining $23.07 is city tax paid at the property.

hotels.name: Ara Maris Hotel & Spa
hotels.blurb: Confirmed, as two bookings with a room change on Sep 4: Deluxe Sea View for the first four nights ($5,249), then a Superior for the last ($1,114). Breakfast included and free cancellation on both. Rooftop sky lounge, two pools in the gardens, and the Thala Spa. Adults and children 10+ only.

hotels.name: Nomos Hotel
hotels.blurb: Confirmed — Superior Double in the Regola, four minutes from Campo de' Fiori and two streets from Hotel Trame, so the trip ends where it started. Nothing prepaid: €530.40 settled with the hotel.

driversNote: Almost the whole trip is car-free: a private driver in from FCO, the Frecciarossa up to Florence, a two-day rental for Tuscany, then rail to Naples and a driver over the peninsula to Sorrento, where everything after is a ferry. The car is collected on Aug 29 on Borgo Ognissanti — just outside Florence's ZTL, eight minutes on foot from the W — and returned to the same desk on Aug 31 before the train south. Two driving days, not fourteen. The IDP ships by Aug 3; pack it with the physical licence even though it's only needed that once. Never drive into a historic centre — Florence's ZTL alone is ~€200 a crossing. Castelfalfi has its own parking, and you have no car on the coast at all — which is the right answer for Sorrento in September. The Sorrento–Positano–Amalfi ferries run mid-April to mid-October, so the whole window is covered, but any of them can be cancelled for weather — keep the hotel's driver number as a backup for the Amalfi day.

bookings.item: PAY FOR SORRENTO BY AUG 6 — the automatic payment failed
bookings.detail: Vio could not set up the card for the four-night Deluxe Sea View, so it has to be paid by hand: $5,087.62 by Aug 6 at 15:00. If it is not paid the booking cancels itself, and that is the room for four of your five coast nights. The one-night Superior on Sep 4 ($1,073.77) is on the normal automatic schedule for Aug 10 and needs nothing from you. Local fees of $161.38 and $40.35 are settled at the property, in euros.

bookings.item: Rental car — cancel the old FCO booking, rebook Florence Aug 29 → 31
bookings.detail: Two problems in one. The old reservation is still FCO Aug 24 → FCO Sep 6, so left alone it bills you for a fortnight's hire you will not take. And the car you do need — Borgo Ognissanti, Florence, Aug 29 to Aug 31 — is not booked at all. Re-quote before cancelling; the old €1,087.81 was a fourteen-day FCO round trip and will not carry over.

bookings.item: Pitti and the Uffizi (Aug 28), and the Accademia (Aug 27) if you want it
bookings.detail: Pitti and the Uffizi are the two with no second chance, so book those first: the 8:15am Pitti opening is what gets Boboli done before the heat, and the Uffizi is guided at 12:15pm after the walk down from the palace. The Accademia is now optional — it sits between a train that can be late and a 4:30pm dome slot that cannot move, and has to be out by 4:15pm. Book it anyway if you want the shot at David; at about €16 each it is cheap to write off.

bookings.item: Horseback riding, lunch & winery — San Gimignano, Aug 30
bookings.detail: San Gimignano Experience, 11am–3pm, ~€120pp: an hour in the saddle through vineyards and olive groves, then lunch, a cellar tour and tastings. A small-group tour, so it fills. Meets at the Bivio Volterra bus stop.

bookings.item: Rome opera — All Saints' Anglican, Aug 25 — CONFIRM THE PROGRAMME
bookings.detail: Still unconfirmed and still unbooked, and the whole evening of the 25th is built on it. Check the Aug 25 programme is actually posted, then book. If there is no concert that night, say so and the evening becomes a long dinner instead.

bookings.item: Galleria Borghese — reserved, card charged Aug 23
bookings.detail: Booked through GetYourGuide for Aug 26, 1:00pm: skip-the-line entry for two with an English audioguide, $113.22. Nothing is paid yet — the card on file is charged automatically on Aug 23, so check that card actually works, given what Vio's did. Free cancellation until 1:00pm on Aug 25 if the day has to change.

bookings.item: Campania Express — Naples ↔ Sorrento, Aug 31 and Sep 5
bookings.detail: €18pp each way, and it does need booking: the Campania Express is a reserved-seat service, unlike the ordinary Circumvesuviana. Out on the 17:26 from Napoli P. Garibaldi on Aug 31, back on the 10:20 from Sorrento on Sep 5. Chosen over a private driver (~€140 a leg) and over the ferry — the ruled-out list says why.

bookings.item: Florence opera — La Traviata at St. Mark's, Aug 28
bookings.detail: A chamber staging in a small church, so the room is small too. Closes the single full Florence day, after the walk back through the centre.
Picks you up in Amalfi after lunch, waits at Ravello's gate (the town is car-free), and drives you back over the pass. Roughly 2 hours of driving. Leave Ravello by 5pm to hold the 7pm rule.

Pierluigi Aug 25 · Da Enzo Aug 26 · Borgo San Jacopo Aug 27 · Sostanza Aug 28 · La Via del Sale Aug 29 & 30 · Cora Bistrot Aug 31 · O'Parrucchiano Sep 1 · Il Buco Sep 2 · Da Gemma (lunch) Sep 4 · Aroma at Palazzo Manfredi Sep 5. Aroma and Il Buco are the two that need the most notice. Night one is takeaway from Emma, so there is nothing to reserve on the 24th.

bookings.item: Ravello Festival — check the Sep 4 programme
bookings.detail: The festival runs to Sep 5, so your Ravello day is inside the window. A concert on the Villa Rufolo stage is the one thing worth reshaping the evening for — but it means a 1h30 drive back to Sorrento afterwards.

bookings.item: Capri ferry — Sorrento → Capri return, Sep 2
bookings.detail: About 25 minutes each way from Marina Piccola, a twenty-minute walk downhill from the hotel or a short taxi. Book both legs online the night before and note the last sailing back. The round-the-island boat can be picked up at Capri's Marina Grande on the day.

Both from Sorrento's Marina Piccola, seasonal but well inside the window. Two or three morning departures down the coast and two or three back in the afternoon — check the current timetable close to the date, the schedules shift with the season.

bookings.item: Pantheon entry — Aug 24, on the Heart of Rome walk
bookings.detail: The Pantheon is no longer free: EUR5 a head, with timed reservations at busy times. Aug 24 is a Monday and the walk reaches it mid-afternoon, so a walk-up will probably be fine — but booking removes the only queue on an otherwise unticketed day.

bookingsRuledOut.reason: No open night in the schedule for a Verona detour — every night from Aug 24 to Sep 5 has a hotel booked elsewhere.

The right register for arrival night — cool rather than formal, six minutes from Trame, open kitchen and a courtyard garden — but it is closed on Mondays and Aug 24 is a Monday. Still available if you would rather move it onto the Wednesday in place of Da Enzo; that would cost you the Trastevere dinner.
Slotted in when Armando fell through, then reconsidered — a 1518 trattoria is characterful but it is not a step up. Worth keeping in mind as the classic-Roman option if Emma is full.

Fully booked for Aug 24 — it seats about forty and goes weeks ahead. La Campana takes the slot: same era of Roman cooking, a room that can seat two at short notice, and closer to the Etabli aperitivo.

bookingsRuledOut.item: Naples → Sorrento by private driver (~€140 each way)
bookingsRuledOut.reason: Door to door and about an hour quicker on Aug 31, but the Campania Express leaves from the same building the Frecciarossa arrives in and costs €36 for the two of you instead of €280 for the pair of transfers. Nothing on either day is tight enough to be worth the difference.

The prettier way, and only 45 minutes on the water. But both legs need a taxi across Naples to Molo Beverello, which is the one part of this trip that depends on Naples traffic. Inbound it means catching the 17:15 within fifty minutes of the train landing; outbound the 12:00 puts you at Centrale around 13:10 for a 13:30 Frecciarossa. And Marina Piccola is uphill from the hotel where the station is flat. There are already three ferry days on the coast.
Dropped in the replan. Naples is now a change of trains on the way down and on the way back — the five nights it would have cost go to the single coast base instead.

bookingsRuledOut.item: Volterra, and a second Tuscan wine estate
bookingsRuledOut.reason: Tuscany is two nights. San Gimignano and the horseback vineyard tour fill the one full day there.

bookingsRuledOut.item: Positano or Amalfi as the base
bookingsRuledOut.reason: Both are beautiful and both are stairs. With one of you working four days out of five, Sorrento wins on flat ground, a real town, fibre, and ferries to everywhere else on the coast.

budget.note: 5 hotels, 13 nights — all five now booked. Trame ($1,588), The Hoxton Florence ($693, room only), Castelfalfi ($2,132), Ara Maris Sorrento ($6,363 across two bookings with a room change on Sep 4), Nomos Rome ($658). That is $664 under the $12,098 the earlier plan carried.

Rail is booked and firm: €1,000 for the two of you across all three Frecciarossa legs in Executive (€290 Rome–Florence, €450 Florence–Naples, €260 Naples–Rome), about $1,080. Naples↔Sorrento is the Campania Express both ways, €72 the pair, against roughly €280 for private drivers. The rest is still estimate — FCO driver, a 2-day Florence–Tuscany rental car, ferries to Capri, Positano and Amalfi, the Amalfi→Ravello→Sorrento driver, and taxis.

Vatican, Caracalla and the Galleria Borghese, the Florence galleries (Accademia, the guided Uffizi, Pitti and Boboli) and the Duomo, two operas, the Capri round-the-island boat, Villa Cimbrone and Villa Rufolo, and the San Gimignano horseback/lunch/winery tour (~€120pp, ~$260 for two). Three lines are now real prices rather than estimates: the Brunelleschi Passes are bought and paid at €60 the pair (~$65), the Vatican came in at €90 for two (~$97), and the Galleria Borghese is reserved at $113.22 for two with an audioguide, charged automatically on Aug 23. Held at $2,115, but it now carries slack rather than running tight — the Vatican was costed here as the private early-entry guide the plan originally called for, and the booked group tour is a fraction of that. Worth re-baselining once the Florence galleries are booked and their real prices are in.

shopping.note: Answering Hanji's question directly: the best quality-per-euro on this walk is Falconeri, and the reason to buy Italian luxury here rather than at home is roughly 10–20% off US prices before you claim the VAT back. Everything mapped below is in Rome, because Rome is where this trip has shopping time — Day 1 at five, and Day 3's lunch is five minutes from Monti.

vat.headline: Claim it — the threshold just dropped
vat.detail: Non-EU residents can reclaim Italian VAT on any single shop's receipt over €70.01, down from the old €154.94. The rate is 22%, but after the refund operator's commission you actually see 11–15% back. From 1 July 2026 Italy switched to a single passport-based validation, so the FCO desk should be faster than older guides suggest. Get the form validated by customs BEFORE check-in on Sep 6 — after you have checked the bags, the goods are gone and so is the refund.

places.name: Falconeri
places.sells: Cashmere, silk and merino knitwear, men's and women's
places.why: The answer to the question. Pure cashmere, made in Italy, at a price the same quality does not reach in the US — the group behind Calzedonia buying a Trento cashmere house is why. Two minutes off the Corso, and there is a second branch at Via del Corso 404.

places.name: Calzedonia
places.why: Cheap without being disposable — tight assortment, constant rotation, and the stitching outlasts the price.

places.name: Intimissimi
places.sells: Lingerie, cotton and modal basics, pyjamas
places.why: Same group as Calzedonia and Falconeri. The basics are the buy; prices are noticeably below the US stores.

places.name: Rinascente
places.why: The efficient option if the afternoon is short: most Italian labels under one roof, a tax-free desk in the building so you are not chasing forms, and a rooftop bar with an aqueduct running through the basement.

places.name: Via dei Condotti
places.why: The reason to buy Italian luxury in Italy is arithmetic, not romance: no import duty, and 10–20% under US shelf prices before the VAT refund. Brioni and Battistoni are the Roman tailoring houses rather than the global names.

places.name: Via Borgognona
places.why: The same register as Condotti with a fraction of the crowd. Worth the detour purely for being able to move.

places.name: Via del Corso
places.street: Piazza Venezia to Piazza del Popolo
places.sells: The high-street spine — OVS, Zara, and the chains
places.why: A mile of mid-market shopping and the walk's backbone. OVS is the Italian one worth a look; the rest you have at home.

places.name: Bulgari
places.why: Roman, and on this street since 1884 — the flagship is the shop, not a branch of one. Bold colour and architectural forms lifted from the city itself.

places.name: Via del Boschetto
places.why: The opposite end of the scale from Condotti and the better story: makers at street level, working in the window. Five minutes from Wednesday's lunch.

places.name: Via Urbana
places.why: Small independents and young labels, the part of Rome that is not selling to tourists.

places.name: Mercato Monti
places.why: WEEKENDS ONLY — and your Monti day is a Wednesday, so this one is a miss unless the plan changes. Noted because it is the thing everyone recommends.

places.name: Via del Governo Vecchio
places.why: Rome's vintage street, and it sits directly on Day 1's Heart of Rome walk between Campo de' Fiori and Piazza Navona.

elsewhere.name: Florence — leather
elsewhere.detail: Scuola del Cuoio behind Santa Croce is the real thing; the San Lorenzo market stalls mostly are not. Time is tight on both Florence days, so treat this as opportunistic.

elsewhere.name: Florence — Ponte Vecchio gold
elsewhere.detail: Goldsmiths have held the bridge since 1593. You cross it twice on Friday, between Pitti and the Uffizi.

elsewhere.name: Naples — coral and cameo
elsewhere.detail: Carved at Torre del Greco just south of the city, and the one thing on this list you cannot buy better anywhere else. You pass through Naples twice — Aug 31 and Sep 5, both times with a train to catch.
